comparison: Both evaluate tonotopic organization in TR neurons (C3, C55, C57, C59) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses specifically on TR tonotopy with statistical validation, while peer review combines this with CT lack of tonotopy (C4, C56, C58) as a unified finding about 'degradation of tonotopic organization.' Both find the evidence convincing.

Both evaluate the absence of tonotopy in CT neurons (C4, C56, C58) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this as a separate finding with appropriate statistical tests, while peer review discusses it together with TR tonotopy as the core finding. Both reviewers affirm this central result without challenge.

Both evaluate frequency tuning heterogeneity claims (C5, C68-C78) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary analyses and spatial gradients, while peer review notes initial clarification requests about IQRBF interpretation that were later resolved. Both accept the findings after revisions.

Both evaluate broader tuning/bandwidth in CT neurons (C79-C90) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights multiple metrics and notes the unexpected BWmax finding, while peer review initially requested clearer FRA categorization criteria but later confirmed concerns were addressed. Both accept the bandwidth characterization.

Perfect overlap on intensity tuning claims (C92-C100). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of statistical tests and regional differences, while peer review offers implicit acceptance through lack of specific commentary, suggesting the findings were uncontroversial.

Both evaluate projection-specific vs layer-specific controls (C65) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes C65-C67 as critical controls for conceptual advance, while peer review notes C64-C65 were specifically requested by Reviewer 1 and later accepted. Both recognize importance for establishing projection-specific organization.

Both evaluate projection-specific functional organization (C66-C67) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this with C65 as demonstrating projection identity determines properties, while peer review notes this addresses Reviewer 2's concern about layer vs projection specificity. Both accept this as evidence for projection-specific organization.

Perfect overlap on methodological explanation for imaging discrepancies (C63, C117-C120). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes reconciliation of contradictory observations with established knowledge, while peer review offers implicit acceptance through overall finding acceptance. Both find the explanation consistent with cited literature.

Both evaluate viral labeling methodology and validation (C36-C40, C47, C111-C116). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes functional validation and chronic imaging stability, while peer review highlights the novel rabies virus approach as a key strength and notes experiments were 'well executed.' Both affirm methodological validity.

Both address sample sizes (C51-C54). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with adequate samples, while peer review notes the observation that CT neurons outnumber TR neurons but does not challenge validity. Peer review comment appears observational rather than critical, ultimately accepting the findings.

Both evaluate functional interpretation claims (C128-C133, C135) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are reasonable hypotheses requiring additional experiments (behavioral, perturbation), while peer review notes uncertainty about importance outside behavioral context and questions about intensity-dependent tonotopy. Both recognize speculative nature beyond direct data.

Both address regional tonotopy analysis (C62). OpenEval includes this with other CT tonotopy claims as SUPPORTED, while peer review implicitly accepts through lack of challenge. The regional analysis supports the main conclusion about absence of CT tonotopy.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization claims (C102-C110) about L6 neuron composition and comparison to L5 findings as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These claims provide important interpretive context for understanding the projection-specific approach.

Partial overlap on CVS labeling validation (C111-C116). OpenEval emphasizes chronic imaging and prior literature validation as SUPPORTED, while peer review focuses more on the novel methodology as a strength (C36-C40). Both affirm the approach but emphasize different aspects.

OpenEval evaluates interpretation claims about single-cell studies and classical literature (C122-C126) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These claims contextualize findings within prior work and explain differences from previous studies.

OpenEval evaluates main conclusions (C136-C137) as SUPPORTED, noting direct experimental support for lack of CT tonotopy and conceptual support for projection-specific organization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviews affirm the overall findings throughout.

Peer review evaluates anatomical localization methods (C41-C45) as SUPPORTED through implicit acceptance. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses these anatomical methods, though OpenEval R1 includes C45 in broader methodological evaluation.

Peer review evaluates TR neuron labeling restriction to minimize ambiguity (C48-C50) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses this methodological decision, though OpenEval R1 includes C49 in broader methodological evaluation.
